notes.text:
This update for go1.26 fixes the following issues:

Update to go 1.26.10 (bsc#1255111):

- CVE-2026-78663: net/http: double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams (bsc#1284770).
- CVE-2026-78669: net/http: excessive CPU consumption from repeated initial window changes (bsc#1284772).
- CVE-2026-111943: crypto/x509: mitigation for security concerns with a specific Certificate Authority (bsc#1286317,
  bsc#1286261).

To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

notes.text: The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.
